## Detailed entries

### Aberdeen

- **Type:** City
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** 2026-07-20 (City Council first reading and passage, 7-0)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-07-20` (exact)
- **Duration:** Extended by Resolution 26-10-01R to 12:01 a.m. local time July 1, 2027, or the earlier effective date of an ordinance amending the zoning regulations to regulate data centers.
- **Current end date:** `2027-07-01`
- **Sectors:** data center, cryptocurrency mining
- **Moratorium ID:** `sd-aberdeen-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Resolution No. 26-07-04R adopted July 20, 2026, as amended by Resolution No. 26-10-01R adopted October 19, 2026.
- **What prompted it:** City's current zoning/building regulations and staff may not adequately address data centers; council found officials 'hampered' in assessing permit applications, creating unpredictability and risk of stranded investment pending a comprehensive study
- **Affected projects:** None named; as of publication Aberdeen had not received a specific data center development proposal for City Council consideration.
- **Detailed status:** Resolution 26-10-01R, adopted October 19, 2026, extended and modified the original moratorium; it states a July 1, 2027 sunset at 12:01 a.m. local time or the earlier effective date of a qualifying zoning ordinance. Later actions and present force as of November 5 have not been independently established. [VERIFY: operative interval, later amendments/extensions/repeal, judicial developments and current legal force.]
- **Outcome:** Original resolution passed July 20, 2026; extension Resolution 26-10-01R adopted October 19, 2026, 9-0.

### Pennington County

- **Type:** County
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2024-11-19 (Board of Commissioners unanimous vote); effective 2024-12-12; extended one additional year by unanimous vote on 2025-10-21
- **Normalized date:** `2024-11-19` (exact)
- **Duration:** Original Ordinance 741 specified expiration November 18, 2025 unless extended and took effect on completed publication. The board voted unanimously October 21, 2025 to extend it; the August 25, 2026 Rapid City Journal reported an end date of November 18, 2026. The adopted extension text has not been verified.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** wind, solar
- **Moratorium ID:** `sd-pennington-county-2024`
- **Legal basis:** Pennington County Board of Commissioners temporary zoning moratorium on utility-scale wind and solar development, adopted unanimously November 19, 2024 (effective December 12, 2024); extended unanimously October 21, 2025 through November 18, 2026, while an alternative-energy task force and the Planning Commission draft amendments to zoning ordinance Section 3-17 (renewable energy systems)
- **What prompted it:** More than 450 citizens petitioned for a moratorium after the Planning and Zoning Commission approved conditional-use permits (2024-10-28) for the Cheyenne River Ranch Wind and Solar Farm near New Underwood
- **Affected projects:** Cheyenne River Ranch Wind and Solar Farm (7 miles south of New Underwood, 30 miles southeast of Rapid City), which received conditional-use permit approval October 28, 2024 that triggered the petition and moratorium.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. Pennington County's temporary zoning moratorium on utility-scale wind and solar development (enacted unanimously November 19, 2024, effective December 12, 2024, after 450+ citizens petitioned against the Cheyenne River Ranch Wind and Solar Farm's conditional-use permits) was extended unanimously by the Board of Commissioners on October 21, 2025 through November 18, 2026, to give an alternative-energy task force (formed March 2025) and the Planning Commission time to finish a consolidated ordinance amending zoning Section 3-17. A related but legally separate zoning-ordinance amendment permanently barring utility-scale wind and solar from agricultural (non-industrial) land passed its second and final reading 3-2 on August 18, 2026, after a multi-month back-and-forth (first reading May 19, 2026; delayed multiple times); commissioners indicated the moratorium could be lifted early once the Planning Commission's consolidated ordinance is finalized.
- **Outcome:** Extended by unanimous vote on October 21, 2025 (moved by Commissioner Derr, seconded by Commissioner Hadcock).

### Turner County

- **Type:** County
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Extended
- **Date enacted:** 2025-08-26 (Turner County Board of Commissioners adopted Ordinance #100-25, a temporary zoning ordinance, 4-0 with the chairman recused, per official minutes)
- **Normalized date:** `2025-08-26` (exact)
- **Duration:** One (1) year (Ordinance #100-25, effective on completed publication); extended one year by Ordinance #105-26 (adopted 2026-08-25) to expire 2027-08-25
- **Current end date:** `2027-08-25`
- **Sectors:** wind, solar
- **Moratorium ID:** `sd-turner-county-2025`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance #100-25, 'A Temporary Zoning Ordinance Regulating Utility-Scale Alternative Energy in All Turner County Zoning Districts' (adopted 2025-08-26); extended by Ordinance #105-26, 'A Temporary Zoning Ordinance Extending the Moratorium Regulating Utility-Scale Alternative Energy Systems in All Turner County Zoning Districts' (adopted 2026-08-25); SDCL 11-2-10, 7-18A-8
- **What prompted it:** Proposed Swan Lake Wind Project (NextEra Energy Resources; up to 97 GE turbines, approximately 248 MW) spanning Turner and Yankton counties; county sought time to study and regulate before the project could proceed
- **Affected projects:** Swan Lake Wind Project (NextEra Energy Resources), spanning Turner and Yankton counties; NextEra withdrew its application for the project in or around August 2026.
- **Detailed status:** County minutes record Ordinance 105-26 adoption August 25, 2026, with a one-year extension and express August 25, 2027 expiry unless sooner repealed, amended or extended. They print September 3 publication and September 23 effectiveness, while the original 100-25 expressly expires August 25, 2026. Continuity and the publication/effectiveness discrepancy require review. Scope is utility-scale alternative energy including solar and wind, not established here as a data-center restriction. [VERIFY: operative interval, later amendments/extensions/repeal, judicial developments and current legal force.]
- **Outcome:** —

### Yankton County

- **Type:** County
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-07-21 (County Commission adopted the moratorium 5-0, recorded as Action 26248C)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-07-21` (exact)
- **Duration:** Six months from adoption (approximately to 2027-01-21); the commission packet draft had proposed 12 months, but the adopted motion changed the term to six months
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, cryptocurrency mining
- **Moratorium ID:** `sd-yankton-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Yankton County Resolution No. 26-7, 'Resolution Establishing a Temporary Moratorium on the Acceptance of Applications, or Issuing of Permits, for Approval of Building, Planning or Use Permits for Data Collection/Storage/Processing or Bitcoin Mining Facilities Exceeding a Power Capacity of 250 kW,' passed and approved 5-0 on July 21, 2026
- **What prompted it:** Concern about incoming data center and Bitcoin mining facility proposals; commission wants time to draft permanent siting standards
- **Affected projects:** None named; resolution addresses applications and permits for data centers or Bitcoin mining facilities exceeding a power capacity of 250 kW. Whether the threshold qualifies both categories requires interpretation.
- **Detailed status:** Published Resolution 26-7 records July 21, 2026 passage, 5-0, immediate effect after passage and approval, and six consecutive months unless extended. The unsupported 180-day conversion and January 17 endpoint are cleared. No independently verified later-action or current-force conclusion. [VERIFY: operative interval, later amendments/extensions/repeal, judicial developments and current legal force.]
- **Outcome:** Enacted six-month moratorium after an initial motion for a 12-month term failed for lack of a second.

### HB 1005 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `sd-hb-1005-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Kent Roe; R
- **Recorded status:** Deferred to the 41st legislative day by House State Affairs on 2026-02-04 (Yeas 9, Nays 3); no further action recorded (bill died).
- **Provisions:** Would have provided a 50-year sales and use tax exemption for specified enterprise IT equipment and software used in qualified data centers, subject to facility and qualifying-date requirements, electric-cost-shifting safeguards and water-provider notice. The proposed data-center definition excluded digital-currency mining.
- **Mechanism / scope:** incentive_support; fiscal
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://sdlegislature.gov/Session/Bill/26317/291571>)

### HB 1038 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `sd-hb-1038-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Chair of the House Commerce and Energy Committee at the request of the South Dakota Public Utilities Commission; Committee bill
- **Recorded status:** House passed 60-5 and Senate passed as amended 32-2; House concurred in Senate amendments 67-0 on 2026-03-10. Signed by the Governor on 2026-03-24; the final session index records that signature in its 2026-03-30 entry. The act prescribes no effective date; 2026-07-01 is inferred under SDCL 2-14-16 as the regular-session default, subject to constitutional and statutory veto and referendum provisions. Later amendments, referendum effects, and current legal force have not been verified.

### SB 135 (2026), Data Center Bill of Rights for Citizens

- **Policy ID:** `sd-sb-135-2026-data-center-bill-of-rights-for-citizens`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Chris Karr and Rep. Jon Hansen (prime sponsors); additional Senate and House co-sponsors listed in the legislative index; R
- **Recorded status:** Senate passed as amended 34-0 and House passed as amended 60-7; Senate concurred in House amendments 33-1 on 2026-03-10. Signed by the Governor on 2026-03-24; the final session index records that signature in its 2026-03-30 entry. The act prescribes no effective date; 2026-07-01 is inferred under SDCL 2-14-16 as the regular-session default, subject to constitutional and statutory veto and referendum provisions. Later amendments, referendum effects, and current legal force have not been verified.
- **Provisions:** Defines data centers at 10 MW or greater; requires separate electric-service terms and reimbursement of fairly attributed costs, including departure or material load reduction; protects local authority to regulate data centers; requires water-provider notice and compatibility determinations, Board of Water Management allocation limits, and semiannual public water-use reporting.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; mixed
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2026-07-01
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://mylrc.sdlegislature.gov/api/Documents/SessionLaw/306613.pdf?Year=2026>)
